payload.rationale: Observed facts: MLB lists Milwaukee at Baltimore on Sep 20, 2026 (23:20 UTC) as Scheduled with no probable pitchers named. Through Sep 17, Milwaukee is 95-58 (.621, +197 run differential, 43-32 on the road) while Baltimore is 75-78 (.490, -26, 36-39 at home). Transfer assumption: converting season-level strength to a single-game probability via a log5/Pythagorean-style approach gives roughly 62-63% for Milwaukee on neutral ground; MLB home advantage (~54% for the home team) pulls this back to about 58-60%. I shade slightly lower to ~57% because late-September context matters: Milwaukee at 95-58 has likely clinched or nearly clinched a playoff spot and may rest regulars or use depth starters, while Baltimore at 75-78 is out of contention but has no obvious incentive change. Single-game MLB outcomes are highly variable and heavily driven by the unknown starting pitcher matchup. Reasons this could be too high: Milwaukee resting starters/bullpen ahead of the postseason, a strong Orioles starter, or the Brewers' record overstating true talent (favorable schedule or luck). Reasons this could be too low: Milwaukee's +197 differential implies true strength above even its .621 record, Baltimore may be playing out the string with callups, and the Brewers' road record (.573) is solid. A postponement pushes settlement but does not change the win probability much; cancellation/void is excluded from scoring.
limitations: Starting pitchers, lineups, injuries, and bullpen usage are unknown.
Playoff-clinch/resting-regulars effects in late September are assumed, not observed.
Season records are transferred to a single game via generic models; home advantage and schedule strength are approximated.
Standings are as of Sep 17; games on Sep 18-19 could shift context slightly.
